svg.title: Backtracking
svg.desc: Backtracking. Build a solution one choice at a time and undo any choice that hits a dead end: N-Queens, sudoku, permutations. Step 1, Choose, check, go deeper: Place a queen in row 0, then try row 1 until a square is safe. In row 2 every square is attacked. Step 2, Undo the last choice: Undo the last queen and try its next square; when a row runs out, undo one more. Solution: 1 3 0 2. Step 3, Pruning is the point: Each attacked square rules out every board below it: 114 of the 256, with only 26 squares tried. Step 4, When the tree explodes: (a+)+b against n a's with no b: 2^(n−1) ways to split them, so each extra a doubles the work.

g.text: Place a queen in row 0, then try row 1 until a square is safe. In row 2 every square is attacked.
Undo the last queen and try its next square; when a row runs out, undo one more. Solution: 1 3 0 2.
Each attacked square rules out every board below it: 114 of the 256, with only 26 squares tried.
(a+)+b against n a's with no b: 2^(n−1) ways to split them, so each extra a doubles the work.
r0c0 is safe: place a queen
r1c2 is safe: place a queen, go deeper
row 2 has no safe square: dead end
r2c1 is safe: place a queen
row 3: all four attacked, dead end
row 1 used up: undo r1c3 and r0c0
all 4⁴ = 256 boards with one queen per row, in search order
each a after the first can stay in the group
or start a new one: two choices per a
its search tree: every way to split the a’s
32 ways to split 6 a’s, and every one fails: no b
a regex in a firewall rule
linear-time engines: RE2, Go regexp, Rust regex
